analysis: The supplied PR units are documentation and changelog only: two added changelog.d/*.md files and a docs/architecture/inference.md edit. No executable source is included, so the described behavior changes cannot be verified here. Documented changes: (1) GLM-5.3-Flash now accepts `strict` tool declarations, validating each auto tool call against its schema before exposure instead of constraining decoding; (2) returned OpenRouter `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` text is rendered as `reasoning_content` in history, with summary and encrypted entries skipped; (3) empty-string tool-call arguments are read as `{}`; (4) null reasoning/thinking controls are treated as unset and `thinking` is accepted as a Boolean or object; (5) variable-frame-rate video is indexed by presentation order at i / nominalFrameRate, followed by the unchanged 2 FPS sampler. Docs state that contradictory switches, `preserve_thinking`, forced tool choices, hidden reasoning and unknown reasoning members remain refused. The docs keep the existing 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (`maximumDecodedBytes`), the 28,532 visual-token cap and media exclusion from prefix lookup and capture. Those bounds and the cache-isolation posture of T-041/SEC-035 therefore appear unchanged. Relevant threats: TB-007 and T-041 (prefix cache excluded for media, unchanged); A-001 (prompt content, with reasoning text now re-rendered into the prompt); and the TB-003 media-handling threats, with T-050 as the closest. Unverified integration questions for a code-bearing review: (a) that the video frame-count and decoded-byte caps are enforced before decoding with the nominalFrameRate-based timing, so a crafted VFR clip with a misleading average rate cannot bypass limits or cause large allocations; (b) that `ToolConstraintValidation.validate` fails closed for strict tools, with no unvalidated tool-call exposure; (c) that returned-reasoning rendering does not enable prompt-injection of template control tokens beyond what `reasoning_content` already permitted. These are not findings, because no code was supplied. No threat-model assumptions are shown to be invalidated.
